question: When do we consider that two medications are bioequivalent ?:

options.opa: The pharmacological effect of both is identical.
options.opb: The pharmacological effect and the bioavailability are the same.
options.opc: The speed of disposition (Cmax and Tmax) and the bioavailability of the active principle are practically the same.
options.opd: The speed of disposition (Cmax and Tmax) and the clearance of the active principle are practically the same.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bioequivalence defined" -> "medications have similar pharmacokinetic properties" -> "Cmax and Tmax are comparable" -> "bioavailability is similar" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Bioequivalence criteria" -> "pharmacological effect must be similar" -> "bioavailability must be the same" -> "Cmax and Tmax must be similar" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Two medications compared" -> "Cmax and Tmax measured" -> "bioavailability assessed" -> "if both are similar, they are bioequivalent" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Bioequivalence assessment" -> "clearance rates compared" -> "Cmax and Tmax evaluated" -> "if similar, medications are bioequivalent" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bioequivalence involves" -> "pharmacological effect comparison" -> "bioavailability analysis" -> "Cmax and Tmax evaluation" -> "if all are similar, they are bioequivalent" -> 90%
analysis: Bioequivalence is determined by comparing the pharmacokinetic parameters of two medications, specifically focusing on their bioavailability and the rate of absorption (Cmax and Tmax). Therefore, the correct option is one that addresses both the speed of disposition and bioavailability.
